key_gap: Both reached the same design (trolley-battery on the 8 km ramp + 5 diesel trucks; $17.25M capex, ≈ 5 yr payback, −11,600 t CO2/yr), but the human derived it from an explicit conflict-axis analysis — the positions disagreed about WHERE fixed infrastructure is acceptable (rigid high-energy ramp vs flexible grid-less work), not about diesel-vs-electric — and that axis produced the synthesis's boundary condition (grid capacity < 60% of ramp demand or horizon < 6 yr → collapse back to diesel). The AI's frame opened binary (diesel vs BEV), found the partition by enumerating a third alternative in HOW, accepted the 60% share as given rather than derived, and added the boundary only in REVIEW, where it remained residual risk rather than a design condition.
learning_signal: For any significant decision with two live positions, the decisive dialectical move is to construct each side in its strongest form, name the axis on which they conflict, and test whether partitioning along that axis yields a dominating alternative that preserves BOTH core interests — the human's synthesis contained an explicit element serving each camp (cheap zero-tailpipe energy where energy is spent; infrastructure-free mobility where infrastructure is impossible). The AI produced the same artifact without producing the method, so it missed the boundary condition that the axis makes obvious.
suggested_improvement: Add an explicit adversarial-pair step in WHY/HOW for decisions with ≥ 2 live alternatives: construct the strongest form of each side, name the conflict axis (the dimension that separates the positions), and generate a 'partition along the axis' candidate before selecting; when a partitioned/integrated alternative is selected, require a mandatory packet field 'synthesis boundary' — the falsifiable condition under which the integration collapses back to the either/or.

key_gap: The dialectical baseline forced a synthesis — 'merge B's funnel into A's, share one back office, $600k each' — that papered over a non-convex threshold: below $1.0M the enterprise sales org cannot exist and below $0.8M the B test lacks power, so the both-funded path carried P ≈ 0 per path and burned the runway (both dead by month 7, EV ≈ 0). The AI kept the thresholds as hard constraints from WHAT onward, falsified the split in two lines of arithmetic (0.6 < 1.0, 0.6 < 0.8 → EV ≈ 0 vs $4.2M), committed to A, and used a bounded parallel probe as insurance (P 0.65 → 0.72, EV $4.64M) without turning it into a third path.
learning_signal: Synthesis is legitimate only when the constraint set is convex — when the conflict is a continuum. When either side carries a minimum effective dose (threshold), integration without commitment is a mirage: the correct move is to name the either/or, commit by EV, disclose the sacrificed side as a real loss, and buy insurance (bounded probe/reserve) rather than average the budget. Treating a hard threshold as a 'budgeting artifact' is the style's signature failure and is detectable in advance by a threshold check.
suggested_improvement: Add a THRESHOLD CHECK gate in HOW before selecting any integrated/combined alternative: test whether the resources to be shared fall below either side's minimum-effective level (split invalid if so); if thresholds exist, force an explicit commitment decision whose packet names the sacrificed alternative as a real loss, and prefer bounded parallel probes or reserves over partial funding.
